newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close lower as buying interest waned.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close lower as buying interest waned.

text.p: Shares ended in the negative as buying interest waned ahead of the weekend break, analysts and dealers said.
At the close, the Composite Index was down 10.21 points, or 1.01 percent, at 1,002.63.

Telekom, which underpinned the market's rise in the morning on a strong rebound, fell back just ahead of the release of its half-year results later on Friday. The stock ended unchanged at 9.70 ringgit after earlier rising to 10.0.
"There's no good news on the news front. Telekom is expected to report single-digit growth," said a local house analyst.
The market has not been able to sustain an upward momentum due to recent currency volatility and concerns that Malaysian interest rates were heading higher.

"Blame the ringgit. Interest rates are going up," said a dealer at J.M. Sassoon. He said news that the central Bank Negara has asked local banks not to raise their base lending rates was helpful but not exciting. "Otherwise, the banks will get squeezed around the neck," he said.
Economists said the Bank's move will stop banks from raising their base rates to above 10.0 percent. The BLR ceiling in July was fixed at 9.67 percent, unchanged from June.
